critique: The positive theorem delivers finite-sample recover-or-abstain certification only for linear Gaussian perfect variance resets under known, transcript-defined population bands; it neither extends to the broader smooth-intervention class nor derives those bands from more primitive law conditions. The logistic converse proves an exact no-return result at one explicit null, but establishes only the necessity of excluding some weak graph-changing alternatives, not necessity of the proposed bands or a quantitative minimax beta-min boundary. The Gaussian construction separates executed and all-subset margins, but does not show that the published model-specific margin premise can be discarded generally. The polynomial-bit theorem starts from supplied rational covariance and support-frame enclosures, so it does not provide an end-to-end raw-data implementation or reproducible software evidence. These scope and practical-evidence limits preclude flagship status, while the proved certificate, separation family, and adaptive sequential impossibility result support a field-tier contribution; the framing does not falsely claim a matched or sharp boundary.
